abstract: Presents the table of contents of the proceedings.

articleTitle: Author index
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Adaptive cross-layer QoS framework for multimedia traffic in heterogeneous UMTS/WLAN networks
abstract: Achieving acceptable level of QoS cross-layer provisioning for multimedia services in integrated heterogeneous UMTS/WLAN networks is from significant importance. In this paper, an adaptive QoS cross-layer module that provides the best QoS and lower cost for any given multimedia service (by using one or more wireless interfaces at a given time) is presented. The performance of the adaptive QoS cross-layer algorithm is evaluated using simulation with dual-mode UMTS/WLAN mobile stations with cross-layer communication within. The analysis of our framework has shown overall superior performances and QoS provisioning for different multimedia services in a variety of network conditions.

articleTitle: Customized k-space trajectory for compressed sensing MRI
abstract: The paper presents a method for spectrum customized k-space sampling for Magnetic resonance imaging. The proposed k-space trajectory is customized for certain types of Magnetic resonance images. Experimental testing has shown that this sampling method is suitable for compressed sensing MR Imaging because the customized mask captures most of the k-space energy in only a small number of samples.

articleTitle: Microwave soil moisture sensor based on phase shift detection of transmission coefficient in band-stop structures
abstract: In this paper novel miniature microwave soil moisture sensors based on band-stop structures have been developed, which operate at a fixed single microwave frequency. Sensors were designed in microstrip technology for use in wireless sensor networks for measurement and mapping of soil moisture in arable lands. Sensors detect transmission coefficient phase delay which is a function of the soil permittivity that is in turn in direct relation with soil moisture. Two novel sensors are proposed which operate at 2.54 GHz and 2.75 GHz. Both solutions offer two times wider ranges of the phase delay and from three to almost thirteen times greater sensitivities compared to conventional microstrip sensor solutions.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of multi-antenna AF two-way relaying over Rayleigh fading channels
abstract: In this paper, we present the performance of multi-antenna harmonic mean amplify-and-forward (HM-AF) relay system over independent and non-identically distributed (i.n.i.d) Rayleigh fading channels. The outage probability, moment generation function and symbol error probability are derived in closed-form using the SNR statistical characteristics. Finally, for comparison with analytical results, we perform some Monte-Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: Intra-subject stride-to-stride variability: Selecting subject's representative gait pattern
abstract: Stride-to-stride variability is well known and important phenomenon often used for estimation of the gait fluctuations and indicative measure for potential risk of falling in elderly. In many gait analysis studies and the descriptions of new processing and analysis methods, the problem of selecting representative gait cycle is solved with choosing one gait cycle from the middle of the recording sequence, or averaging several cycles from the middle. In this paper, we describe stride-to-stride variability based on data from inertial sensors. We suggest a simple, mathematical method, how to select stride which best represents the subject's gait pattern.

articleTitle: ABER performance of dual-hop system over asymmetric fading channels with interference at the relay
abstract: This paper studies the performance of a dual-hop amplify-and-forward (AF) system where the source-relay and relay-destination channels experience Rayleigh and Rician fading, respectively. The relay node is corrupted by Rayleigh faded multiple co-channel interferences. Based on proposed system model, new closed-form expression for the average bit error rate (ABER), in the case of several modulation formats, is derived. Numerical results are performed in order to verify analytical approach.

articleTitle: Realization of high quality RF inductors using LTCC technology
abstract: This article offers a detail description of design, simulation, fabrication and characterization of buried inductors on two different substrate configurations intended for application in the radio frequency range. The presented inductors are meander type structures fabricated using LTCC (Low Temperature Co-fired Ceramic) technology. Different substrate configurations incorporate placement of an air-gap beneath the inductor. Obtained results present over 25% increase in quality factor and widening of the operating frequency range by over 45% in comparison with inductors on standard substrate configurations.

articleTitle: Rolling stock location data analysis using an immune algorithm on an intelligent embedded device
abstract: Objective of this paper is to design an intelligent rolling stock safety system on an embedded device which could provide a way for railway transport to avoid dangerous situations, examine the algorithms used in artificial immune systems and ways how they can be used together and provide data for each one other. The authors review analysis methods used to detect, predict and control undesirable rolling stock travel conditions.

articleTitle: Exact bit error rate of QAM over Nakagami fading channel
abstract: In this paper, we derive the new closed-form expressions for bit error rate (BER) in detecting quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) signals transmitted over flat Nakagami-m fading channels. By using this expressions, the effects of fading severity and average signal-to-noise ratio on BER perfomance are analyzed.

articleTitle: The capacitive divider power supply and its design problem
abstract: Capacitive divider power supply is a well-known circuit. Still, it has not been paid attention to among researchers and is still lacking a thorough analysis and referred optimal design guidelines. We give the formal time-domain equations describing the behavior of the supply, as well as the estimation for the circuit's dissipation, that will be used as a foundation for a further research.

articleTitle: Analysis of single-phase PLL with novel two-phase generator for grid-connected converters
abstract: It is very important for proper work of grid-connected converters to have accurate detection of phase angle, frequency and amplitude of grid voltage. Estimation of these grid parameters can be achieved using PLL (phase locked loop) based on SRF (synchronous reference frame) theory. This PLL should have robustness against noise and offset introduced by measurement and data conversion. This paper proposes an improved PLL alorithm that has excellent noise and offset rejection property. The main part of the proposed PLL is a novel two-phase generator which is used to obtain two quadrature signals for SRF block and PI regulator in closed control loop.

articleTitle: Proposal of a modern SCADA system architecture
abstract: This paper discusses some of currently the most challenging problems of SCADA system design, and presents a possible architecture of a general purpose SCADA intended for high-end applications. The paper gives proposal of a new architecture, which relies on basic principles from the old implementation, adapted and perfected to fulfill the needs of the modern market. Some of the basic requirements for implemented SCADA system includes scalability, distributed and reliable networked operation, high capacity/performance in real time, and support to future extensibility of the solution and implemented data model.

articleTitle: Improvement of children safety by using RFID based service
abstract: Most important characteristics of RFID technology, the way it operates and basic components are presented in the paper with the aim to be used for kid's safety. This study shows the proposed implementation of the system solution based on RFID and deployed in school that registers arrival and departure times of pupils and sends that information to parents via SMS and/or e-mail. A survey is conducted among potential users to evaluate a need for implementation of this system in Belgrade schools.

articleTitle: The practical design of in-vehicle telematics device with GPS and MEMS accelerometers
abstract: Latest generation of vehicle tracking devices relies not only on Global Positioning System (GPS) but also uses a low-cost Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) accelerometers. This combination supports new services as driving style characterization and Automatic Crash Notification (ACN). Focus will be on practical considerations of such telematics unit. Work will consider boundaries of allowed errors and minimal requirements for sensors and mounting requirements. Sensor range for crash detection and impact angle estimation was tested on field trials with two units containing accelerometers range of 18g and 2g. Kinematic orientation of vehicle is evaluated in series of field trials with resulting standard deviation of estimation of 1.67°. The second run of experiments considers dynamic range and sampling rate of sensors during collision. Sensor range of 8g (typical for current telematics devices) can be used to detect crash without accurate knowing of impact angle.

articleTitle: Algorithm for acoustic camera with post processing analysis
abstract: Acoustic camera is usually used for identifying the dominant noise source. Commercial version is easy to use and in many cases gives satisfactory results. However, high complexity of the sound sources, their movement, and their spatial distribution often present difficulties during the identification of the dominant noise source. Older versions of acoustic camera can not provide an acoustic image of the moving sources. The inability to record targets in motion renders old versions useless, when faced with a task of recording actual traffic or identifying a sound that is spreading from certain parts of the vehicle. To be able to analyze moving objects new acoustic camera algorithm was designed. During the design process few different algorithms have been investigated. Advantages and disadvantages of algorithms are discussed and the algorithm for sequential signal analysis which gives the ability to track moving targets is outlined.

articleTitle: On the Minimal state tuple of VNET with overall QoS guaranties
abstract: A definition of overall telecommunication network performance is presented. A model of overall virtual telecommunication network (VNET), with QoS guaranties for Class 0 traffic (Real-time, jitter sensitive, high interaction: VoIP, Video Teleconference), is considered in stationary state, taking into account details of the users' behaviour. The approach described allows reducing the number of system describing parameters from over 260 (System Tuple) to 9 parameters: 8 static and one dynamic. This Minimal Tuple set and the correspondent equations described look as the minimal possible information for the overall telecom network performance modelling. The system of 9 equations presented, allows easy finding the all, important for overall network dimensioning/re-dimensioning, dynamic parameters.

articleTitle: Evolution strategy to make an objective function in two-phase ILP timetabling
abstract: Evolutionary strategy is here used in searching objective function for two phase integer linear programming approach to solving the school time tabling problem. This allows improvements in generated timetables even for criteria, which are not easily expressed by ordinary objective function.

articleTitle: Advanced level-crossing sampling method
abstract: We propose an advanced signal-driven sampling method that uses the level-crossing sampling technique based on the selected signal sampling and non-uniformly distributed quantization levels. The number of the quantization levels is chosen to compress the volume of sampled data. The proposed sampling method is targeting sporadic signals. The trade between the accuracy of the recovered signals and the compression ratio is evaluated.

articleTitle: Wavelet image decomposition based variable density compressive sampling in MRI
abstract: This paper considers compressive sampling in magnetic resonance imaging. The structure of the sparsity domain is analyzed and based on the conclusions, probability profile for random sampling is proposed. This probability profile divides the k-domain into tiles with constant probability for sampling. The value of the probability for sampling k-space frequencies in every tile is found based on the content of the specific image or similar images. The performance of the proposed probability profile is compared to the performance of the distance based probability profile.

articleTitle: Efficient bandwidth of 50 GHz fiber Bragg grating for new-generation optical access
abstract: Authors have measured differential group delay of fiber Bragg grating band-pass filter with 50 GHz full width half maximum bandwidth with method based on Jones Matrix Eigen-analysis and have evaluated efficient bandwidth employing 2.5 Gbit/s and 10.3125 Gbit/s optical signals to draw out limitations for realization of dense wavelength division multiplexing-direct broadband access system.

articleTitle: Application of multi-quantum well RSOA in remodulation of 100 Gb/s downstream RZ signal for 10 Gb/s upstream transmission
abstract: We investigate the possibility of remodulation of downstream 100 Gb/s signal into the upstream 10 Gb/s signal using multi-quantum well reflective semiconductor optical amplifier. Theoretical model used for analyzing carrier and photon dynamics in device takes into account forward and backward propagating amplified spontaneous emission noise. We present results for various downstream signal waveforms and different detector integrating times. The analysis shows that by increasing detection time, bit-error rate can be improved.

articleTitle: One solution of audio/video grabber architecture used for automatic testing of Set Top Boxes
abstract: Modern TV technology, especially digital television today is equipped witn smart computer based TV signal receivers. This document shortly describes the hardware architecture and base functional principle of audio/video grabber device, used for automated testing of Set Top Boxes. Audio/video grabber is a part of BBT testing environment.

articleTitle: Forensic analysis of encrypted volumes using hibernation file
abstract: Nowadays, software tools are commonly used to encrypt data on hard disk. Those tools keep encryption keys in system memory to provide the user easy access to plain text of encrypted files. Key possesion enables data decryption. A procedure that includes usage of hibernation file as a source of memory content is described. Publicly available tools are used to perform the procedure. The procedure is successfully tested on a system that uses current encryption program.

articleTitle: Digital guitar tuner
abstract: Digital guitar tuner is a tool widely spread in today world of music. It is designed for tuning the instrument in conditions where tuning “by ear“ is not possible. This paper shows a realization of guitar tuner as an application programmed in JAVA, Eclipse Platform version 3.3.2 programming language. Realization is based on using comb filters and Goertzel algorithm for spectral analysis.

articleTitle: Using radio irregularity for increasing residential energy awareness
abstract: Radio irregularity phenomenon is often considered as a shortcoming of wireless networks. In this paper we present the method of using radio irregularity as an efficient human presence detection sensor which increases user awareness in smart homes. The idea is based on monitoring the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) between stationary wireless (2.4 GHz — Zigbee) power outlets. When a human enters into the existing radio communication field, the signal can be absorbed, scattered or reflected by the body what results in strong variations of RSSI. Based on the detected changes compared to the initial values, the system detects human presence and responds with the automatic control of any appliance connected to outlets. Compared to conventional sensors, the proposed solution preserves the sensorial intelligence, simplicity and low installation costs without need for additional devices integration.

articleTitle: System design for storage distributed system inside local network
abstract: The need for data storage is related to the very beginning of digital data processing. Data were first stored on floppy disks, magnetic tape and at the end on hard diskc. Today, in order to save data we can use some of traditional storage systems like DAS, NAS, SAN, Client server systems and peer to peer systems. Peer to peer systems have resources which they share with other peers on network. Existing peer to peer systems are based on WAN connection links, implementing overlay network in order to achieve connectivity with logical addressing scheme. The most important issue that peer to peer systems have to provide is availability of data using some sort of replication and redudancy. Usually this is implemented using file replication or erasure code. In this paper we will present design of peer to peer based distributed system for data storage inside local computer networks, with file replication. File replication relies on introduced algorithm for storage management.

articleTitle: Performance of turbo super-orthogonal space-time frequency trellis coded OFDM system
abstract: Turbo codes with iterative decoding are known for its astonishing low bit error rate performance. In this paper, we investigate the performance of turbo super-orthogonal space-time frequency trellis code (TurboSOSTFTC) in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) system over frequency selective fading channels (FSC). The coding scheme is based on parallel concatenation of two SOSTTCs, interleaving and multiple-transmitter/ receiver diversity systems. The frame error rate (FER) of the TurboSOSTFTC scheme is evaluated by computer simulation over different channel scenarios. It is shown that the TurboSOSTFTC-OFDM performs better than conventional SOSTFTC-OFDM and TurboSTTC-OFDM systems over the same channel condition.

articleTitle: Integration of PRINCE2 model into ITIL V3 model
abstract: PRINCE2 is the most popular methodology for the project methodology in ICT industry and ITIL V3 is the most popular methodology for organisation management or service management. The paper shows results for a implementation of 2 new services in IPTV system for a standard third phase of ITIL V3 service lifecycle and results for a new performed third phase of ITIL V3 service lifecycle which is a result of integration of PRINCE2 model into ITIL V3 model. The paper compares results from these 2 measurements and then concludes in which parameters is a new model better than the old one.

articleTitle: S-method based eigenvalue decompositon for analysis of multicomponent communication signals
abstract: An application of the eigenvalue decomposition method to the multicomponent communication signals is considered in this paper. The method is tested on the synthetic and real signals and it provided efficient components segmentation and localization. Namely, it is shown that is possible to separate all the components of interest within the observed signal.

articleTitle: Utilizing CUDA architecture for improving application performance
abstract: Graphic card processors have a vital role in that they bring parallelism to a whole new level. Applications need to do a large amount of calculations in parallel. In this paper numeric calculation performance comparison between executing numerical calculations in traditional processor and the graphics processor using CUDA architecture is presented.

articleTitle: Application of the Affine Fourier Transform based multicarrier system in aeronautical satellite channels
abstract: The fast growth of the wireless data transmission requires reliable and high data-rate modulation techniques that can cope with impairments of the time-varying multipath channels. The current demands are aimed at using the Internet anytime and anywhere. The main constraint to achieving these demands is the mobility. Suppression of Doppler spreading effects caused by high velocity of moving objects represents a challenging task. Hence, in this paper we present an application of multicarrier system based on the Affine Fourier transform (AFT-MC) for transmission in aeronautical satellite channels. We analyse the AFT-MC in terms of interference suppression, spectral efficiency, data rate and bit error rate (BER) in aeronautical satellite channels. It will be shown that AFT-MC has good performance in aeronautical satellite channels.

articleTitle: Videoconferencing in the complex e-learning scenario
abstract: Videoconferencing can be used to enhance complex e-learning scenarios, especially beneficial when learners or professors involved in e-learning scenario can be described as “digital immigrants”. Example of the complex e-learning scenario implementation with the use of videoconferencing is presented, targeting Serbian K-12 teacher population as learners, through their professional development course about the “Modern concepts of programming”.

articleTitle: Engset loss models for an OBS/OPS node with shared wavelength conversion
abstract: Asynchronous bufferless OBS/OPS core nodes behave as loss systems and therefore, widely analyzed under traditional Erlang and Engset loss models. Additionally, it has been shown that the Engset traffic assumptions are more realistic with a correction in the offered load. This correction is proposed due to the fact that in case of loss, the source cannot offer a new packet while the input wavelength is busy in transmitting a lost packet. This effect is more evident in OBS switches which deals with large burst lengths compared with packets. In this study, Engset traffic model with and without correction in the offered load is used to analyze a switch using the shared wavelength conversion. We show that the degree of wavelength conversion also effect the blocking of the switch significantly and in the switches with small and medium port counts the effect of blocked inputs due to packets/bursts should not be ignored. Continuous time Markov chains have been used for analysis and expressions have been derived to evaluate the time, traffic and call blocking.

articleTitle: Design of optical filters based on multiple ring resonators operating in C and L bands
abstract: In this paper the design of optical filters operating in C and L bands is presented. The well-known generalized approach based on Mason's rule and delay line signal processing has been implemented for modeling multiple ring resonator architectures in Z-domain. Interesting results have been obtained about free spectral range up to 17 THz and very low cross-talk (-16 dB) in the overall transmittance function.

articleTitle: One solution of realization of TV application for digital TV
abstract: The paper presents a realization of TV application for digital TV receiver. It has been developed for ST 5167 SOC patform, using Comedia TV middleware. The ralized system has been verified using TV application for Linux Ubuntu on PC platform. The paper also contains description of TV application stack and data structures used for transmision of digital TV data.

articleTitle: Application for WALK activity and ECG monitoring on mobile devices based on Android OS
abstract: In this paper, we present a telemedicine application for mobile devices based on Android OS platform. The basic applications functionality of ECG transmition is extended to the real-time ECG analysis and step detection using acceleration sensors integrated in mobile phones. Application is integrated in the existing telemedicine system using predefined interfaces.

articleTitle: Evaluation of an XML database based Resource Directory performance
abstract: In this paper, an implementation of a Resource Directory, a directory storing descriptions of resources available in an Internet of Things system, based on a native XML database is described. Its performance is compared with performance of a Resource Directory with the same functionality, but implemented using a relational, SQL database. The evaluation results show hat the XML based Resource Directory provides more flexible management of the resources and shorter response time.

articleTitle: Sources of uncertainties in power line communication system modeling
abstract: The aim of this paper is to develop a theoretical model of medium and high voltage cables used for the purpose of power line communication from the point of view of uncertainties. The equivalent circuit of power line communication cable is described along with its uncertainties. We have considered uncertainties since their propagation causes errors in modeling power line communication and in measuring the signal sent through the power line.

articleTitle: Attacks on the RSA cryptosystem using integer factorization
abstract: This paper describes how integer factorization algorithms may be used to break the RSA cryptosystem. Complexity and efficiency of Trial division, Lehman's method, Pollard's ρ method and Quadratic Sieve algorithm are analyzed. The corresponding numerical results are presented for typical secret key lengths.

articleTitle: Estimate of probability detection of the new hydroacoustics system for measuring hydroacoustic signatures of floating objects
abstract: This work describes results in development of the functional model of a new hydroacoustic system for detecting and processing hydroacoustic signals of floating objects. The developed system has a possibility to record digital acoustic signatures (fingerprints) for different types of floating objects. Under water field of the float objects is considered in the area of water space where exist hydroacoustics preassure as result of many activities on float object. This system belongs to the group of passive detection systems that don't show one's own presence in watery surroundings. The work gives a new way for further developments of the software and hardware, giving a possibility for the identification types of floating objects. For that purpose, this work describes estimate of probability detection of the system. The work gives relevant parameters as P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>, P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">fa</inf>, SNR(z), C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>=SNR(y)=6,19 dB, diagrams, t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">fa</inf>, DT<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Hz</inf>, as well as tabulated values of indices and threshold of detection.

articleTitle: E1 services availability in EMS SDH network
abstract: In the paper is given availability analysis of telecommunication network build on synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH) and optical ground wires (OPGW). We have examined three special cases which characterize network availability, with real values of failure rates. It is given availability dependence on repair times for multiplexer and cable and basis on previous operating experience, review of existing status and suggestions for improvement. We have reconsidered the classical E1 service. Charts of the modeled paths are given at the end.

articleTitle: Voltage controlled oscillator with regulated power output in the UHF band
abstract: The paper presents designs of two oscillators, both with a buffer amplifier and a bandpass filter: one with a voltage controlled oscillator and a wide-band filter, and one with fixed frequency oscillator and a narrow-band filter. The work includes the results obtained by software simulations, the assembly of individual parts, and measurements of the complete circuit.

articleTitle: Test stream generation framework for video quality assessment methodology evaluation
abstract: This paper describes functional framework for generation of test streams for evaluating the performance of visual perceptual quality models. The paper proposes structure and system support for the realization of system, with a goal of creating streams which tend to represent variations in quality of video material distributed over IP networks. Quality can be impaired under several circumstances, such as artifacts resulting from encoding video material with some of the coding schemes, signal propagation through the transport medium and its interference with the environment. For the proposed functional framework basic structure and system support is developed, consisting of components for generating impaired, but also unimpaired multimedia streams in different formats and functional simulation of the entire chain of multimedia system to the point of displaying the content on the end-user devices.

articleTitle: Compact dual band CPW-fed monopole antenna with L-strips for WLAN/WiMax applications
abstract: A novel dual band CPW-fed antenna with symmetrical L-strips is presented for WLAN and WiMax applications. The proposed antenna is composed of a square ring feedline with a pair of L-strips added to it for building the radiator structure. By employing these strips, antenna can yield two different resonances to cover the desired bands while maintaining small size and simple structure. Based on this concept, a prototype of antenna is fabricated and tested. The experimental results show that the antenna has the impedance bandwidths of 930 MHz (2.48-3.54 GHz) and 290 MHz (5.12-5.41 GHz), which can cover both WLAN in the 5.2 GHz band and WiMax in the 2.5/3.5 GHz bands.

articleTitle: PodBoard: Podcastmg braced blended learning environment
abstract: Podcasting as a social technology endorsed integrating push based mobile learning (m-learning) and pull based electronic learning (e-learning) into push-pull blended learning (b-learning), which gets the students involved in the development and reception of course podcasts, and thus feel a higher level of social presence and achieve better academic results. Podcasting impact differs in societies and countries, it is one of the motivations and outcomes of this work. PodBoard, a blended learning environment is implemented, its performance is evaluated using Task Technology Fit (TTF) model. Results based on Egyptian students responses are presented.

articleTitle: Automatic classification modulation based on sixth order cumulants of various structures
abstract: In this paper process of AMC based on sixth order cumulants with one conjugation is analyzed. Different channel conditions with white noise only and multipath propagation with pre-defined impulse response are considered separately. The results of classification performance are compared with results of AMC alghoritm with sixth order cumulants with three conjugations. Based on achieved results, new hybrid alghoritm has been proposed in order to improve classification results. Superior perfomance of this new algorithm is confirmed through Monte Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: Application of Katz algorithm for fractal dimension in analysis of room impulse response
abstract: Analysis of the room impulse response is main problem in room acoustics. Here we propose using Katz fractal dimension for analysis of room impulse responses, applied on Schroeder curve. The methodology used in this paper together with the obtained results shows some of the possible directions in the application of fractals in room acoustics.

articleTitle: Bagging algorithm for pixel classification
abstract: In this research, Bagging algorithm that incorporates different classifier into classifier ensembles models for pixel classification is suggested. We chose classifier ensembles with decision trees, as the base classifiers. In the problem of pixel classification, experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the Bagging with forest of random trees (RandomForest) as base classifier compared to other methods.

articleTitle: Perception of distortion in duration of voices /š, č, ž, dž, c, r, 1/
abstract: This research aims to determine the boundaries of typical/atypical duration of phonemes /š/,/č/, /ž/, /dž/, /c/ /r/, /1/ based on identification functions of probability of perceptual detection of typical/atypical duration. These phonemes are located in initial position in isolated words /šuma/ (forest), /čelo/ (forehead), /žaba/ (frog), /džep/ (pocket), /cica/ (no translation), /riba/ (fish), /lice/ (face), respectively. Series of tests were conducted in which experts in speech-language pathology gave their opinions on typical duration of stimulus which were pre-modified with Praat software package. The results obtained in the form of ranges of typical duration of the analyzed phonemes will improve speech and language practice.

articleTitle: Performance modelling of MAC protocol for GPRS
abstract: This paper presents the analysis and performance evaluation of the Radio Link Control/Media Access Control (RLC/MAC) protocol in General Packet Radio Service (GPRS) networks. The aim of our study is to model the Media Access Control protocol that provides coordinated access to the shared channels resources of GPRS radio interface. After describing a simple functional model for a single node in GPRS system, a detailed analysis is presented to model the behavior of a single GPRS cell. A Markov chain is developed to describe the single cell system and the expressions for the uplink throughput and mean transfer delay are derived using this Markov chain.

articleTitle: Low computing complexity frame synchronization for OFDM communication
abstract: The paper deals with a new frame synchronization scheme for OFDM systems. The scheme is based on the computing of the detection window variance. The variance is computed in two delayed times, so a modified Early-Late loop is used for the frame position detection. The proposed algorithm has good properties regarding the choice of the algorithm's parameters since the parameters may be chosen within a wide range without having high influence on system performance. The verification of the proposed algorithm functionality has been performed on a development environment using universal software radio peripheral (USRP) hardware. The experimental results are compared to the simulation results, where the simulated system was an equivalent OFDM system with ideal time synchronization.

articleTitle: Reducing the emergency call setup duration in UMTS
abstract: During a UMTS (Universal Mobile Telecommunication System) call setup, one part of the signaling messages is sent on a DL (Downlink) 13.6 kbps and UL (Uplink) 13.6 kbps and another part is sent on DL3.4/UL3.4 kbps. The change of the signaling rate from 13.6 kbps to 3.4 kbps occurs after the RRC (Radio Resource Control) Radio Bearer Setup message. In this paper a new method, called `Delay of Activation Time Method', is proposed. When applied, then most, if not all, of the messages that are exchanged during a call setup are sent on a signaling rate of DL13.6/UL13.6 kbps. It follows that the duration of the signaling messages affected by this method is four times shorter than in case of prior art. In this paper, the application of the proposed method, on an emergency call setup that triggers an A-GPS location procedure, is measured.

articleTitle: Multi-user interference performances for PPM-TH-UWB systems
abstract: Ultra wideband (UWB) communication system proved to be a new and reliable system for wireless communication due to its capacity to provide low power, short range high data rate, fade free, relatively shadow-free communications in a dense multipath environment. We will analyze multi-user interference (MUI) performances for pulse position modulation with time hopping (PPM-TH-UWB) system for different number of users and different rate bits.

articleTitle: TV controlled via Android application
abstract: This paper describes an research of alternative ways of controlling of modern TV device. Used methods, experimentally research and development applications for devices based on Android operating system. Connecting TV devices and devices based on Android operating system is done through a wireless network, messaging is implemented over standard TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) and UDP (User Datagram Protocol) protocol. The achieved result, an Android application that implements one of the alternative management TVs.

articleTitle: Modeling of Faraday cage for electromagnetic-compatibility testing
abstract: By military standards, electromagnetic-compatibility tests of tools and weapon systems and military equipment are carried out in a Faraday cage, which has many parasitic resonances. In order to improve these tests, we modeled a complete Faraday cage. Various imperfections of the cage were detected by comparing results of simulations and experiments, and they were included into the model.

articleTitle: Employing relay ordering in incremental amplify and forward Relaying technique to improve outage probability
abstract: This paper investigates the incremental relaying technique with a proposed smart relay selection protocol over cooperative diversity networks based on Amplify and Forward strategy. It is aimed to use bandwidth effectively with the use of a single bit that is feedback by the destination. In fact whenever a direct link from the source to the destination is not satisfactory for decoding (with acceptable BER), the destination requests the help of a set of suitable relays. Since reliability is one of the important issues in wireless network design, using suitable relays in cooperation leads more robustness and reliability of a wireless communication network based on cooperative diversity because cooperation only with one relay is not more reliable. The performance of the proposed method is derived in terms of BER, the outage probability.

articleTitle: Improving the vertical handover latency for VoIP between WLAN and WiMAX networks
abstract: In this paper we study the optimization of the parameter Link Going Down that affects the vertical handover performance when mobile node moves with different speed from WLAN to WiMAX network. We show here that optimizing the Link Going Down parameter for VoIP traffic can appreciably improve the vertical handover latency. This is very important for real time services like VoIP, where minimal handover disruption and service continuity are the primary requirements. We also verified our simulation results theoretically with an equation that relates the optimized link going down factor with the speed of the mobile node.

articleTitle: Evaluation of mobile video streaming in heterogeneous wireless networks
abstract: Recently, the number of mobile users equipped with wireless devices capable of video streaming on the go has increased immensely. The trend follows the ever expanding choice of multi-access wireless technologies to which they connect and the growing popularity of mobile video applications. In this paper, we evaluate mobile video streaming over heterogeneous wireless networks. We design and implement a hybrid evaluation framework consisting of a testbed network and an emulator. We focus on the network-layer quality of service (QoS) for multihomed mobile hosts moving at pedestrian or vehicular speeds across WiMAX and Wi-Fi networks. Extensive experiments are carried out running the widely adopted MPEG-2 standard and the current MPEG-4/AVC standard of increasing dominance. Experimental results present the performance of mobile video streaming in different scenarios depending on the user's movement speeds and video coding standards. It is further demonstrated that MPEG-4/AVC outperformed MPEG-2 in terms of throughput, packet delays, packet loss and jitter.

articleTitle: A 6.36mW CMOS Ultra-Wideband (3.1–10.6-GHz) LNA in 0.18-μm for UWB pulse-radio systems
abstract: This paper presents an Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Low-Noise Amplifier (LNA) which its frequency range is from 3.1 to 10.6 GHz using 0.18-μm CMOS at 25°C. Simulation results show that the IIP3 is about 1dBm at 6GH and the Noise Figure (NF) ranges from 3.41-4.47 dB over the band of interest. Input matching is better than -12.81dB, S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> below -27.51 dB, S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sub> below -13.05 dB, S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> 10.16 ± 1 and the power consume is 6.36mW at 1V supply voltage. The proposed LNA topology is very suitable for UWB pulse-radio system applications.

articleTitle: Foot movement classification based on signals from accelerometer
abstract: The assessment of achieved function is essential for both the follow up of therapy and feedback for assistive system. In this paper we present one method of the data processing for signals coming from the inertial sensor. Specifically, we address the assessment of the foot movement; we applied k nearest neighbors classification technique for extracting information regarding qualitative description of the movement. The ankle joint was chosen because it plays a major role in walking, and it needs to be controlled very often in persons after stroke. We investigated influence of foot movement dynamics on classification error. Results suggest a high level of accuracy, which is in the classification. The methods are presented by using the measurements in healthy volunteers. Healthy volunteers were selected in order to create the benchmark that will be later used for assessment of the function in patients with gait abnormalities (e.g., stroke patients).

articleTitle: Software implementation of data compression algorithms and their comparative analysis
abstract: In this paper, software implementation of most commonly used data compression algorithms is described. The application is developed in programming language Delphi 6, it allow testing of Shannon Fano, static and dynamic Huffman as well as Lempel Ziv algorithm. As a result of the application, efficiency and compression level of chosen algorithm is calculated, and comparative analysis of multiple algorithms for the same data sequence is also allowed. User can enter data and read the results using graphic user interface. In order to illustrate the application options, the corresponding numerical results are presented and compared with the results obtained by using commercial data compression tools.

articleTitle: Redundant GPS time synchronization boards for computer networks
abstract: Nowadays, accurate and reliable time is an essential requirement in computer network based systems. To fulfill this necessity, time synchronization idea has been developed. Meanwhile in some cases, reliable time is so vital, therefore a redundant structure can be used. In this paper, a time synchronization system is investigated by designing and implementing a time synchronization board capable of synchronizing time of computer networks using NTP (Network Time Protocol). A redundant scheme is also embedded in this work to provide more reliability.

articleTitle: Medium access protocol for efficient communication in clustered wireless sensor networks
abstract: An efficient utilization and allocation of the limited resources of a wireless sensor network (WSN) in a way that maximizes the information value of the data collected is a significant research challenge. Within this context, this result concentrates on architectural approach as a means of focusing a sensor's on obtaining the important data at heterogeneous environment. Our goal is to facilitate the development of sensor network with to separate all sensors in distributed clusters. Fully collision-free TDMA-based MAC protocol for a WSN cluster was proposed. As we assume that in each cluster every node is one-hop far from its neighbors it's obvious that no routing protocol is needed and it enables to use very simple sensor nodes with limited resources, which prolongs WSN duty life. Together with upper level content here refers to automatic runtime selection of services implementations and network resources to execute the application specification in a resource-efficient and context-aware case.

articleTitle: Towards improving medical image diagnosis
abstract: In this paper we exploit the unique challenges and at the same time new opportunities of the medical domain, by developing methods with automatic diagnosis capacity. Our methods use the capabilities of the statistical framework for mathematical processing of images and image mining techniques for producing diagnosis rules. The experiments were carried out on a medical database with digestive images.

articleTitle: Comparison of DVB-T/H and DVB-T2 in mobile, portable and fixed TV channels
abstract: The paper deals with the DVB-T/H (Digital Video Broadcasting - Terrestrial / Handheld) and DVB-T2 (Digital Video Broadcasting - 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> Generation Terrestrial) standards and their performance in multipath and fading TV channel models. For the comparison the overview information about DVB-T/H and DVB-T2 were taken from the DVB Facts Sheets and added with according references. Then parameters and models for mobile, portable and fixed TV scenarios were used for system analysis and simulation. Dependences of BER and MER on C/N ratio for all types of payload inner modulations are compared with focus on mobile, portable and fixed TV services availability. Comparison of these two standards performance in various channel models is the main novelty contained in this paper.

articleTitle: Selecting software development life cycle models
abstract: The most common approach to selecting the most suitable software development life cycle model is the expert evaluation. Without a formal guidance such a selection depends too much on expert personality. In this paper the formal framework for selecting the best suitable model is provided. The control mechanism is provided as well. Finally, the approach is tested for the most common models in three different scenarios.

articleTitle: Application of medical information system MEDIS.NET in professional learning
abstract: A large amount of data collected using certain medical information system, among other things, can be used for training health professionals and students of medical sciences. This paper presents possible usage of medical information system MEDIS.NET for increasing professional knowledge of medical workers and students. Education is accomplished by using the results obtained by interactive tools for generating statistical reports (ReportER) and BI tools. At the end of this paper there is a suggestion for developing a central repository and collaboration platform for rare diseases in order to gain knowledge about these diseases, their diagnosis and treatment.

articleTitle: Measuring and simulation electromagnetic field results of wireless router AT-WA1104G
abstract: Because of its practical properties, wireless networking had a great expansion in last several years. However, there were questions about possible electromagnetic radiation of this kind of communication. In this paper, the experimental measuring and simulations results of wireless router AT-WA1104G realized in electrotechnical school Nikola Tesla in Niš were presented as one of examples of insight in electric field strength, magnetic field strength and SAR from wireless router.

articleTitle: Experimental verification of near-field beamforming using low-cost microphone array
abstract: Beamforming or spatial filtering is a technique used for achieving high directivity radiation patterns of sensor arrays. In recent decades it found its acoustic application through the development of acoustic camera and holography. This paper demonstrates the example of near-field beamforming. Eight low-cost microphones array was built and used for signal acquisition and spatial filtering is done by dedicated software. Despite the modest price of hardware components obtained results are solid and accurate.

articleTitle: Searching image database based on content
abstract: The modern age is characterized by great professional and private multi-media production of which the largest percentage are images. Search a large number of images from the user's perspective is almost always based on content. The aim of this work is to create a database search algorithm for images that is content based. Starting from the features matrix, algorithm is based on working with color, texture and shape. Using the five characteristics of color, four characteristics of texture, and one feature for shape, the initial group of images, by applying different levels of ranking and reduction, are reduced to a small number of representative images in relation to query image. Using a neural network model and the group obtained images, the result obtained by artificial intelligence is shown to the user. Interaction with the user, in every iteration, search result can be further filtered or modified in accordance with selected images.

articleTitle: Energy efficiency analysis in heterogeneous network deployments
abstract: Energy consumption of communication networks has recently received increased attention. Although wireless networks account for a rather relatively small share of energy use, lowering their energy consumption appears beneficial from an economical perspective. This paper provides analysis of an energy efficient heterogeneous network deployment. The network incorporates IEEE 802.11b and IEEE 802.16e-2005 network nodes and a two interface mobile node. The evaluation is done through extensive simulations conducted in QualNet simulator. The results analyze the validity of heterogeneous networks deployment in terms of used energy. Additionally, the paper investigates energy consumption trade-offs of a heterogeneous network in contrast to homogeneous network deployment.

articleTitle: Use of optical fibers for UV detection
abstract: In this paper novel fiber-optic UV sensors are presented. U-shaped sensor covered with UV marker for UV radiation detection and fiber-optic sensor with one end covered with powder from mercury lamp. Dependence of output light intensity on distance of sensor with mercury from UV lamp is investigated as well. On the output of the sensor with powder from mercury lamp are obtained peaks of fluorescent emission at approximately 616 nm and 620 nm wavelengths.

articleTitle: Wireless ambient lighting control from TV receiver
abstract: This paper present a conceptual solution, implementation details, results of performance analysis and tests of system for controlling lighting effects from TV receiver over wireless network. The system represents an extension of a home automation system. It is based on embedded computer system that is integrated into the TV receiver, and enables the use of a single central device for monitoring and controlling household devices such as RGB lamps. Lamps are used to provide lighting effects and regulation of user's ambient. For controlling this and other devices user can use a standard remote controller.

articleTitle: A complete system for remote collection of meteorological data
abstract: Weather stations are often need to be set up in places that are far away dozens of kilometers from the center for the processing and displaying of measured data. Facilities on such sites usually do not have a developed infrastructure of wired Internet, and therefore sending data is impossible. The subject of this paper is to analyze and represent system-rounded solution to this problem, using GPRS technology. Implemented system consists of modules to collect and send data on the remote side of the meteorological station and modules for receiving, storing and displaying the results using web interface on server side.

articleTitle: Implementation of digital audio effects for electric guitar on DSP platform
abstract: Starting from mathematical model, following electric guitar effects are implemented: delay, chorus and flanger. Implementation is done on a commercial fixed point single core DSP processor, which has total 24k words data memory, 2k program memory and processor speed of 150 MIPS.

articleTitle: An analysis of medium access control in IEEE 802.11s networks
abstract: In this paper we evaluated performances of IEEE 802.11s networks. In that purpose, we simulated competition for the medium based on EDCA (Enhanced Distributed Channel Access) and MCCA (Mesh Coordination Function Coordinated Channel Access) mechanisms, using programming language C. We analysed and presented achieved simulation results (average throughput for different traffic categories and average packet delay) depending on the number of Mesh stations and the MAF (MCCA Access Fraction) values.

articleTitle: Automated proving properties of expectation-maximization algorithm using symbolic tools
abstract: In many analysis based on estimation the parameters of probability distribution functions, the algorithms are developing for unknown probabilities. Some algorithms are derived starting from previous solutions and algorithms. One very popular algorithm is the EM (Expectation-Maximization) algorithm. The EM algorithm is a starting point for developing other advanced algorithms. Features of EM and other algorithms are observed with the traditional numerical approach. In this paper, we present a new approach of analysis EM algorithm using symbolic processing (specific Mathematica). We automatically derive properties of the algorithm. The knowledge embedded in the symbolic expressions was used to simulate an example system and EM algorithm to generate the implementation code of some critical parts of analysis.

articleTitle: Magnetic resonant modes in a wireless-powered circuit
abstract: A pair of circular loops of the same radius set at a distance form a closed induction circuit. Coupled to a capacitor, these loops form a resonant circuit wherein energy is transported from one to the other. When a current is introduced into one of the loops, it is received by its companion. This is due to the propagation of magnetic waves through the medium, in this instance, atmospheric air of a characteristic impedance.

articleTitle: A case for online real-time barcode readers
abstract: In this paper we are advocating for the development and adoption of mainstream online real-time barcode reading systems that go beyond common current usage scenarios. The goal is to deliver a reliable and accessible alternative to native applications and proprietary readers. As such we analyze resource dependencies and limitations from a fresh and unconventional perspective in relation to the "in-browser" environment. To attain this feat we propose two barcode service delivery systems: the first one, a modular client-oriented detection framework suited for immediate implementation and the second one, a hybrid system designed for complex cloud infrastructures.

articleTitle: Uplink and downlink beamforming in two-way relay networks
abstract: In this paper, we consider a two way relay network containing two single antenna transceivers and a MIMO relay. We consider a two stage design process, first by obtaining soft estimate of the transmitted signal through receiver beamformer and then designing transmitter beamformers. We minimize the relay transmit power (dissipated in the relay) subject to two constrains on the transceivers received signal to noise ratios(SNRs).

articleTitle: Monitoring radiations based on ultra low power Wi-Fi system
abstract: Cosmic rays monitoring became a very studied field nowadays. A smart system for monitoring rays is composed of mobile devices that are able to measure in realtime the fastest particles which are moving in space. In this paper, a reliable, reduced cost and long-life system for monitoring rays is proposed. By integrating Geiger-Muller tube with very low power wireless devices, the system may be used as a mobile system and may send data to computers using Wi-Fi. The reliability of the system is ensured by using different types of software agents which are able to negotiate using smart algorithms in order to solve several situations that may appear during lifetime, as system reconfiguration in failure or join cases, changing channels, device reallocation, monitoring data and so on.

articleTitle: Integrated component of digital signal processing education system implemented in network environment
abstract: The goal of the research described in this work was to get results about the effectiveness of on-line exercises in the field of digital signal processing, and to develop a set of interactive exercises in purpose of enhancement of the education of this subject as well as to faciliate integration of the subject in an on-line program of distance education. Web pages, and a set of exercises realized in Matlab was created. Appache Web server and Matlab Web server are linked and installed with a database to enable the formative evaluation of the system. During the development of the learning system exercises were accessible via Internet and testing was accomplished through surveys filled by the students. Results of the surveys served to make the evaluation of the learning system. Data were assessed and interpreted.

articleTitle: A solution for improving human resource management in services company
abstract: Our paper developed a business process modeling solution for human resource management in services companies. We link personality types to several abilities, grouped in two categories: minimum abilities and transferable abilities and follow individual performance and transferable abilities in recruitment and promotion process for a call center company. Campaigne indicators for case-study company was obtained using a SaaS solution.

articleTitle: A new sliding mode controller for TCP congestion control
abstract: In this paper a new controller for congestion problem in TCP networks has been proposed. Sliding mode controller is robust against modeling uncertainties and disturbances. In sliding mode control states should be reached a predefined surface (sliding surface), in a limited time and remain the same surface over time. Moving on the sliding surface is independent of the uncertainties, so this technique is one method of robust control. After applying controller to system, stability of the system with controller has been proven by Lyapunov stability criteria. Simulation result shows the efficiency of the sliding mode controller in different scenarios.

articleTitle: Modeling of EM wave propagation in the vicinity of the human body by the use of WIPL-D software
abstract: By the means of numerical simulations using WIPL-D Pro software, some aspects of electromagnetic (EM) waves propagation in the close proximity of the human body were studied. Human torso was modeled by a homogeneous dielectric ellipsoid of appropriate electrical parameters. Transfer function between the two antennas on the body as function of their mutual distance, and intensity and polarization of the near field of one antenna on the human body were observed. Frequencies 2.45 GHz and 850 MHz, as two characteristic WBAN frequencies were chosen for the analysis. It was confirmed that on both frequencies transfer function decays approximately exponentionaly with the distance. It was determined that the polarization of the electric field of the antenna on the body significantly varies with the position. It was illustrated that the communication between antennas are established by both direct and surface (diffracted) component of the EM wave.

articleTitle: Techno-economic analysis of GPON and FTTC/VDSL access networks
abstract: In this paper on the specific case is in detail described a techno-economic study of GPON and FTTC/VDSL access networks. Economic indicators, as well as the risk associated with the implementation of both scenarios are obtained using the discounted cash flow and Monte Carlo analyses. Further, the assessment of the moment when operator should expand network from the dense urban area in urban area is performed by a real option analysis.

articleTitle: The influence of the transmission path model on reception of digital TV signals in conditions of mobile reception
abstract: Until the end of 2011. year, in Serbia will begin experimental broadcasting of digital signal second generation standard (DVB-T2) at thirteen transmitting and two repeating (gap-filler) locations. The terrestrial digital television in addition to stationary reception, is planned for mobile and portable reception. At a reception quality of signal the basic effect has model of the transmission path. This paper will be elaborated the influence of the transmission path model, which has a direct influence on the quality of mobile reception.

articleTitle: WebGL implementation in WebKit based web browser on Android platform
abstract: Android OS has gained much popularity in relatively short period, spreading from mobile devices into set-top box, automotive and internet tablet markets. To meet users' growing expectations of multimedia content delivery methods new open standards, like HTML5 and WebGL, are introduced. WebGL is accelerated 3D graphics library for web, based on OpenGL ES 2.0 (hereinafter GLES2). This paper presents one solution for WebGL implementation on ARMv7 set-top box with Android Gingerbread as target platform.

articleTitle: Connecting Linux based Connected TV: Application implementation guidelines
abstract: This paper presents implementation guidelines for application that enables digital TV receiver, running on Linux operating system, to connect to internet protocol based networks. The proposed solution has support for both wired and wireless connection interfaces. In addition to guidelines of possible software solutions for maintenance of network connectivity this paper also discusses some problems that can occur during the development.

articleTitle: Geographic locations retrieval from photos
abstract: This document will consider the possibilities and risks of the use of geographic data included in the photos, as well as techniques for discovering such information, which we have used in practice. Geotag embedded in images and video clips provide lot of possibilities, but can be potentially dangerous from the standpoint of preserving privacy. Since the data is visible to more users, it can be assumed that these users are not aware of the existence of such data. The goal of online services, which we have set to provide visitors an easy and simple way to verify whether the photos include data on geographical location.

articleTitle: SunSpot in sevice-oriented applications
abstract: SunSpots — Java programmable devices with several built-in sensors allow the measurement and transmission of measured values between the Spots as the nodes in the network. In NetBeans development environment support to Sunspot desktop projects was developed. The theme of this paper is to expand the functionality of Sunspot desktop projects to support working with Web Services, which is not currently provided through NetBeans development environment and demonstration of SunSpot's service-oriented inteoperability with Web Services.

articleTitle: Virtual organizations — Integration of ICT strategy with business and organizational strategy
abstract: This paper is about the dependency among information system strategy, business strategy and organizational strategy in virtual organizations. The rapid development of information technology, especially the Internet and web based technologies, enables managers to design and create radically new, technology based organizational structures T-form organization and virtual organization. In virtual organizations, there are a strong relationships and dependencies among company's business strategy, organizational, information and communication technology (ICT) strategy. If the companies would like to exist and to progress in the future, they have to make a real balance among these three strategies, taking in consideration the key role of ICT.

articleTitle: A novel approach for automatic set — Top box menu error free navigation
abstract: This paper describes a new solution for automated error free navigation through the STB menu for effective functional verification of the STB. The proposed testing solution is based on the existing BBT testing system for testing STB, by specially designed functional drivers. The proposed testing solution provides greater testing efficiency and robustness for the STB functional verification.

articleTitle: An implementation of highly narrowband filter
abstract: This paper describes design and prototype implementation of an extremely narrow-bandpass crystal filter. The imperfections which occur within comercially available crystal units were used to reduce the filter structure complexity.

articleTitle: Efficient realization of an octave filter bank
abstract: In this paper we present an octave filter bank. The design of the tree-structured multichannel filter bank has been done using two-channel filter banks. These banks have been used so that the octave bank would have all-pass complementary and power-complementary properties. The design of the banks has been done in MATLAB<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>. The application of designed bank is expected in processing of audio signals. Results of a subjective testing have been included in the paper also.

articleTitle: Control access kernel functionality verification in Set-Top Boxes via popup detection
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach and system for functional verification of the Set-Top Boxes (STB) related to Conditional Access Kernel (CAK) functionality. The proposed solution is built on already existing BBT testing system with supporting audio-video capturing device, in the form of two newly developed functional device drivers. Since the CAK functionality, within the STB with a smart card, can be monitored via pop-ups at the output, the idea of the proposed methodology is to detect pop-up in the output video signal and conclude from it about STB functionality. For this purpose a novel algorithm for pop-up detection has been developed. Specifically, given the specially designed input test sequences and special STB state conditions, the pop-up window is invoked at particular time instance. The reference a priory known appearance of the pop-up window in the output of STB is compared to the detected pop-up from the STB output. Based on this comparison, in specific time intervals, a decision is made about the STB functionality in terms of CAK functionality. The experimental results of the proposed system performance have shown that the testing system is accurate and robust, provided a rough pop-up window model is given in advance or manually developed.

articleTitle: Zachmanov framework as support strategic decision-making
abstract: The environment in which modern enterprises are characterized by one constant — change. In order for a company that could provide an adequate response to them is necessary to dispose of the right information at the right time. Given the extraordinary complexity of the business, it's not so easy. This paper put emphasis on Zachmanov framework, as well as structured and formal way to present the overall architecture and framework for enterprise information system in the enterprise, with the aim of generating diverse and relevant information for strategic decision-making process.

articleTitle: Integrated software tools for support of wireless sensor network applications
abstract: Wireless sensor networks are used for monitoring phenomena using spatially distributed sensor nodes. A wireless sensor network may be far away from a server which collects and processes data from the network. In that case, one or more gateways are used to connect the network to the remote server via TCP/IP or UDP/IP. To speed up testing and deployment of a network, we have developed a simulator which generates packets such as those sent from real sensor nodes and from real gateway. In addition, we have developed a server application and web service for storing and viewing data collected by the network, respectively. In this paper, we describe the wireless sensor network packet simulator, server application and web service, developed at the Institute Mihajlo Pupin.

articleTitle: Hysteresis modeling in electronics
abstract: Hysteresis is a phenomenon encountered in a lot of scientific domains. This paper presents a representation of hysteresis modeling using Preisach algorithm, starting from minimal measured data. Numerical results show a good agreement between theoretical and represented data. Measured data is done for a metro card in case of a transversal and in case of a longitudinal applied field. Presented results represent a starting point for improvement of vectorial Preisach hysteresis models.

articleTitle: Influence of asynchrony on audiovisual perception of speech
abstract: The paper tries to determine the influence of audiovisual asynchrony on perception of speech. Visual information increases intelligibility of spoken words in complex intermodal integration. This integration is very sensitive to existence of asynchrony. Understanding how high the tolerance to asynchrony in our perception is can help in various fields of research. These improvements can be applied whenever transmission of both sound and picture is needed.
